Serialized field names and input-relative access candidates

This workflow, available starting with v0.4.0, connects a literal key and length to an input-relative value in a known function-call model:

xref -b app field validator_to_staged_rewards --json --layout-only
xref -b app field validator_to_staged_rewards --within 0x12340 --json
xref -b app field validator_to_staged_rewards --within 0x12340 \
  --write --min-offsets 2 --limit 64

--within selects the function whose input argument is the layout root. Different functions may receive a containing object, a nested inline object, or a field reference. Their relative offsets have different origins; inspect function, base_argument, the literal key and the static evidence steps. The JSON includes the selected binary's SHA-256.

Candidates show named offsets, related keys, key/value argument witnesses, known static helper rebases, instruction read widths and an addressed-span lower bound. The displayed field order is lexical instruction/call-site order. It does not claim recovered Rust declaration order or every runtime path's order. Exact size, alignment, padding and allocation identity remain unknown. A skipped field or erased/zero-sized value may leave no recoverable offset in optimized code. No offset is inferred from declaration index times an assumed word size.

An optimized JSON form may write the key, a colon, and the value through separate calls. The continuation candidate requires a common symbolic state or a documented reference-cell relationship, CFG dominance, a colon-store witness, and no intervening key on a known path. A reference-cell relationship does not prove that the writer was not retargeted. Such rows explicitly set association_uncertain, carry an unverified_* state-identity marker, and make the report ambiguous. Their evidence is a static pattern rather than a runtime writer/type identity proof. Plain string co-occurrence is insufficient.

The model follows x86-64 SysV integer-register arguments, constant pointer arithmetic, supported scalar loads, stack spills and known direct or resolved RIP-slot helpers. CFG joins retain only equal facts; unsupported CFGs and bounded helper paths remain explicit. Unknown indirect calls, opaque memory changes, aggregate/scalar promotion and other unsupported forms may be missed. Register positions are argument candidates rather than recovered source signatures. Literal-key/value evidence does not prove the code implements Serde, or that two candidates have the same concrete Rust type.

The accessor phase checks each function's accesses relative to the same input root, using the candidate's offset constellation. --min-offsets 2 requires at least two distinct matching offsets; --min-offsets 1 allows weak single-offset matches and labels them accordingly. --write includes accesses that may write the queried offset, including conditional writes. This is a way to reduce unrelated matches, not a type-identity test. --layout-only skips that global phase while inspecting or selecting a candidate layout. Access widths are respected: a wide load/store can cover a field whose start is inside its byte range. One wide instruction covering multiple offsets is explicitly labeled single_span_overlap_not_type_proof; the reported operand displacement and width remain separate from the field offsets.

Code, function, instruction, stack-fact, summary-depth, time and output-row budgets are finite. Coverage/truncation information is part of the report. Missing results mean no candidate under that model and scope, not proof that a field or accessor does not exist.

The integration fixture uses ordinary Serde derives and serde_json in unoptimized and optimized native builds, runtime offset_of!/size_of! oracles, exported entry/mutator symbols, and stripped copies retaining FDEs. Duplicate names in distinct types, Rust field reordering, mixed widths, rename/skip/nesting, a real mutator and a single-offset unrelated writer are separate controls. The fixture adds no custom key-emission helper to force a particular analyzer pattern.
